dossier.public_summary: The 0.8-day dip lines up exactly with the star's strong 0.8-day rotation and spot variability, and its depth changes by more than a factor of three between sectors while the out-of-transit light swings as much as the dips. The long duration and failed density match add to a picture of spotted active-star variability, not a planet.

reasons.why: Large out-of-eclipse modulation comparable to transit depth points to stellar variability or a close binary rather than a planet; flat-bottom transit does not rule out a diluted binary.
Signal period is exactly the stellar spot period in all sectors, not a coincidence; per-sector variability chi2 99.41 indicates spot-driven active star, inconsistent with planet transit.
Depth changes by factor >3 within same pipeline (10458/10544/11886 ppm vs 5718/6189 ppm) – best explained by changing spot coverage/dilution on an active rotator, not a planet.
Transit duration and density implied by the 0.8-d dip do not match the M-dwarf density; large penalty + xgboost planet_rank 0.2 supports false positive.
